programme.desc: Life in the tropical Atlantic, where everything from dolphins, manatees and whale sharks to sunbathing jellyfish thrive in the Caribbean's warm, sheltered waters, fringed by coral reefs and rich mangrove forests. programme.title: The Fairytale Castles of King Ludwig II with Dan Cruickshank
programme.desc: Documentary exploring the aesthetic styles associated with Ludwig II of Bavaria, the king who was considered to be handsome and loved by his people. Dan Cruickshank investigates the mock-medievalism of Neuschwanstein castle and the complex design of Herrenchiemsee, to assess how they are key to learning more about the enigmatic ruler

programme.title: A Year in the Wild
programme.sub-title: Cairngorms, A Year In the Wild
programme.desc: A tour of Britain's largest national park, a land of extremes in the heart of the Highlands, where a diverse range of wildlife including golden eagles, ptarmigan, capercaillie, red deer and crested tits can be found. The programme explores the area through the eyes of people who live and work there, including a mountain guide, an artist, a gamekeeper and a nature writer. Narrated by Hermione Norris

programme.title: Atlantic: The Wildest Ocean on Earth

programme.title: The Art of Spain
programme.desc: Documentary series exploring the influences on Spanish art. The first programme focuses on the Islamic history of the country and the impact it had on its culture, with art historian Andrew Graham-Dixon investigating the debt that modern Spain as well as modern Europe, owe to Moorish Spain

programme.title: Sally Magnusson Remembers - Mastermind
programme.desc: Broadcaster and writer Sally Magnusson takes her seat in the original, imposing 'Mastermind' chair, and shares her memories of her father Magnus' time as the host of one of British television's most enduring quiz shows. She tells the story of how the programme originated, how her father got the job of quiz master, and what it was like growing up as a teenager and having the catchphrases 'pass' and 'I've started, so I'll finish' hurled her way on a regular basis. Sally also reveals how it feels to sit and face questions in the famous chair, and how it came to be that it now lives in her own living room

programme.title: Turner: The Man Who Painted Britain
programme.desc: Tim Marlow presents this documentary drama chronicling the highs and lows of JMW Turner's life, including his tragic childhood, secret affairs and the exhausting extremes to which he pushed himself to capture a unique quality in his paintings. Ross Boatman stars as the artist

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.desc: How America's reluctance to act after the chemical attack caused Syrian rebels to despair, leaving a vacuum that would be filled by the forces of Isis. Obama's conclusion was that there was no scenario where intervention in Syria would give a desired outcome. The president's vision of a Middle East where the youth would create a democratic and free world for itself collapsed

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo is in Lincoln to hear about how Britain's canals fell into decline after the Second World War, and how they're being restored. Michael also investigates poet Philip Larkin's life and work, visiting the University of Hull - where he worked as a librarian. After arriving in York, he plays God in a rehearsal of the Barbers' Play - the Baptism

programme.title: Wainwright Walks
programme.desc: Julia Bradbury explores the work of Alfred Wainwright. In the first programme, she walks to the summit of Haystacks in the Lake District - his favourite fell. Broadcaster Eric Robson assists the presenter as she aims to discover why Wainwright chose to have his ashes scattered there

programme.title: To the Manor Born

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances

programme.title: She-Wolves: England's Early Queens
programme.desc: Helen Castor tells the story of Lady Jane Grey and Mary Tudor's battle to succeed to the English throne in 1553, the first time in the country's history that no male made a claim to the vacant crown. She discovers the troubles that power brought to each woman, with Jane's reign lasting only a few days before Mary struggled to restore Catholic rule to England. Castor also looks back at the reign of Mary's successor, Elizabeth I, who ruled for more than 40 years and is still regarded as one of England's most successful monarchs - but whose triumphs came at a heavy cost

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Historian Sam Willis explores how castles came under threat from the cannon during the Wars of the Roses, before their whole purpose was transformed in the Tudor era when some of the buildings became palaces to impress monarchs such as Elizabeth I. However, just as they seemed to have lost their defensive function the English Civil War erupted. Sam also looks at their legacy and how they remain popular to this day

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?

programme.desc: The first of a two-part investigation into the murder of a 54-year-old in January 2025. Jamie Gawler was found dead in his Hereford flat, sitting in an armchair with a towel draped over his face. The post-mortem revealed blunt force trauma to the head, neck and chest, with almost every rib broken. With no witnesses, the investigating team began to piece together the victim's final days and soon established he had recently allowed a stranger to stay. The police eventually caught up with the suspect, who had been released from prison just six weeks earlier - and had the words 'Natural Born Killer' tattooed across his back

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: The remaining home-bakers face a brand new Bake Off challenge, as Paul Hollywood and Mary Berry challenge them to prove their mastery of classics recipes from the Victorian era. The reign of Queen Victoria is thought to have been the period of history that gave birth to modern baking, and for the signature bake, the contestants are asked to produce a game pie, which gives one enthusiastic competitor a chance to use a genuine antique from 1850. Mary sets the bakers to work on a fruit cake from the late 1800s in the technical, creating a finished product covered in sugar paste and marzipan that should resemble a tennis court. programme.title: Four in a Bed

programme.title: Four in a Bed

programme.title: Come Dine with Me

programme.title: Car S.O.S.

programme.title: Car S.O.S.

programme.title: Grand Designs

A woman with a history of strokes suddenly loses feeling all down one side of her body, while a young woman with diabetes has blood sugar readings that are so high they're off the paramedic's chart

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E
programme.desc: The trauma team at St George's Hospital in south-west London fights to save the life of a young woman involved in a motorbike accident, which has completely severed her right leg below the knee. An 11-year-old boy is brought in after having a prolonged epileptic seizure, and a 19-year-old arrives with a sewing needle stuck in her foot, but she seems more keen on taking advice from her mum in Bulgaria than from the doctor

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E
programme.desc: This edition focuses on the treatment of sport enthusiasts who have had accidents on two wheels. Billy, 19, has been thrown 20ft from his motocross bike during a race, suffering multiple spinal injuries. Teacher Dave, 53, has facial injuries after riding his new bicycle into the back of a stationary car in Richmond Park, while 30-year-old adrenaline junkie and former Royal Marine Richard has badly dislocated his thumb after falling off a bike

programme.title: A Place in the Sun
programme.desc: Jo and Neil are about to start their next big adventure and move from their home in Exeter to start a new life in Lecce in southern Italy. They want a property that has a guest annex to accommodate friends and family, and that's close to the beach so Neil can surf whenever he wants. Armed with a budget of £200,000, Jasmine Harman shows them five properties for them to consider

programme.title: Heir Hunters
programme.desc: The probate researchers look for the relatives of a possible spy who encountered some remarkable people in his life, and an heir to the estate of a woman whose family earned a living working on the railways. Plus, details of more cases in which beneficiaries still need to be found

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The contest begins at the Richard III in Middleham, North Yorkshire, a pub run by husband and wife Ken and Sharon, who become suspicious when one couple check out before breakfast. The village is known for its horse racing links, but one of the competitors, Matt Wilson, has a fear of horses, and another couple are concerned at staying above a noisy pub

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The second visit is to the Court House Unique Boutique B&B in Shelsley Walsh, Worcestershire, where hosts Keith and Lisa Shearin hope to impress. On arrival, Ken and Sharon are blown away by their honeymoon suite and the seemingly low price. Suspicions over price fixing drive Matt and Paul to the internet to verify the room rate, where they discover an anomaly, and despite Keith's best efforts at breakfast, Jo and Louis dismiss it as being too fancy

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The contestants travel to Castley Camp in Otley, West Yorkshire, for the third day of the contest, owned by single mum Jo Stevenson and her son Louis. Some of the guests are horrified by stains on their bedding and dust in their room, while an afternoon boot camp fitness session reveals Keith's competitive side. At feedback, Jo is left fuming over the comments about cleanliness and breakfast

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The final two days see the contestants staying the night at the Lion & Swan in Congleton, Cheshire, run by owner Paul Whyle and manager Matt Wilson. A dirty bathroom and a waterbed cause upset, while some guests are still fuming about previous negative feedback. However, the worst is left for breakfast, when Sharon reveals she has discovered their rooms online at a higher price than they were told, upsetting Keith and Lisa and leaving the hosts determined to clear their names

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The B&B owners meet for the last time to find out what they've been paid and to settle some scores. First up are Ken and Sharon from the Richard III, who want to learn more about what's been causing Jo and Louis to lose sleep. Next, Keith and Lisa from the Court House Unique Boutique B&B want to challenge Matt about the allegations of price fixing and vehemently fight their corner. Needless to say, there is tension in the air and axes to grind, before the winner is revealed

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Dairy farmer's wife and Disney enthusiast Charlene Fry-Henderson hosts the first dinner party in Dumfries and Galloway, where she hopes that her locally reared meat, home cooking, and entertainment involving a plastic cow will secure her the £1,000 prize. Her guests are local radio presenter Tommy Jardine, banker Olive Melville, prison custody officer Tammy Rice and trainee teacher Josh Jones

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Horse enthusiast and banker Olive Melville hosts the second dinner party in Dumfries and Galloway, where she hopes to impress her guests with a crab starter and mousse dessert - but things take a turn for the worse when a conversation about the royal family divides the diners

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Local radio DJ Tommy Jardine hosts the third dinner party in Dumfries and Galloway, and prepares chicken stuffed with haggis - but first he must continue a family tradition and rustle up a sheep for his entertainment. Tommy then tries to impress his guests with a touch of celebrity name-dropping, but young dance DJ and trainee teacher Josh trumps him at his own game

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Trainee teacher and club DJ Josh Jones hosts the fourth night in Dumfries and Galloway, and hopes he can broaden his fellow contestants' palates with his menu of Indian food. He plans lamb pasanda and tandoori monkfish, but Tammy Rice finds something in her glass that wasn't on the menu. However, Josh hopes his disco entertainment might impress the guests enough to bag him the £1,000 prize

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Tammy Rice hosts the final evening in Dumfries and Galloway, hoping to win the £1,000 prize with her no-nonsense approach and traditional Scottish fare. The dinner-party novice rustles up chorizo and cous cous stuffed peppers for her starter and incorporates haggis into her chicken-based main course

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The latest competition begins in Abersoch, north Wales, at NightSky Glamping, run by Angie Howarth and her daughter Caitlin. Things get off to a good start when Sophie and her fiancé Sam lap up the luxury in their safari tent - especially the hot tub - and Morgan falls in love with the view. However, some dusty decorations disappoint Kadir. After a trip to the beach for an afternoon of bodyboarding, Morgan reveals that he isn't a fan of camping

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The second visit of the week is to Johnny Dough's Restaurant with Rooms in Conwy, north Wales, run by Morgan Austin. Angie and Caitlin are stunned by the sights, but a hairy bed gets Kadir's stay off on the wrong foot. The guests are whisked off on a boat trip to enjoy Conwy from the water. As well as loving the landscape, they get a peek into host Morgan's surprising past

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The Royal Oak in the Peak District, run by Kadir Ustun, is the week's third location. Kadir prides himself on the warm welcome he provides, but mould in their respective bathrooms puts off two sets of guests straight away. Fortunately for Kadir, spirits are lifted after a day out caving at a local attraction - the interestingly named Devil's Arse. The next day, the B&Bers are divided over breakfast, with some raving about it while others are left disappointed

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: Sam Harrison and Sophie Germany host the final visit of the week at the Dovecote Inn in Nottinghamshire. Morgan marvels at his room, but Kadir is determined to inspect every nook and cranny after receiving frosty feedback from Sam and Sophie when he hosted. An underwhelming day out touring the village of Laxton is saved only by the hosts' personalities, though later two of the B&Bers have a disagreement over dinner

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: On payment day, Angie and Caitlin are keen to get to the bottom of some cutlery quibbles. Morgan's upset about some cleanliness complaints, while Kadir thinks some of his fellow B&Bers have been unfair by saying they wouldn't return to his B&B

programme.title: Car S.O.S.
programme.desc: Tim Shaw and Fuzz Townshend head off to Huddersfield, West Yorkshire, to rescue a 1992 VW Corrado, a German coupe that, in its time, was one of the fastest small family cars on the road. The car belongs to 37-year-old Ashley, who even went as far as changing his surname to match his car. Sadly, when Ashley fell ill, his car ended up rotting away under a cover

programme.title: Car S.O.S.
programme.desc: Tim Shaw and Fuzz Townshend head to Kent to rescue a much-loved 1973 Dennis fire engine. It used to belong to New Romney station, where firefighter Tony cherished it. He later bought it to restore and to use for charity fundraising. Alas, Tony died from cancer and never completed the restoration and his colleagues have nominated his son James for the Car S.O.S treatment, so that he can see his father's wishes come true

programme.title: Grand Designs
programme.desc: Kevin McCloud follows plumber Jon Martin and ceramicist Noreen Jaafar as they transform a neglected half-acre site in Gloucestershire. However, they are unable to cut down the 27 protected trees on the plot, so their solution is to build a big, modern treehouse with stilts screwed into the earth and balconies that will have views for miles

programme.title: Oti and Richard's South African Odyssey
programme.desc: In the Western Cape, Oti and Richard take on one of the world's most dramatic roads and meet a community of African penguins. Richard gets a taste of Cape Malay culture, while on the dusty roads of the Weskus, there's a display of the Khoisan people's dance traditions. Finally, in the beach town of Paternoster, they sample some freshly caught crayfish

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E
programme.desc: Tree surgeon Paul, 38, is rushed into resus after falling 25ft. He is experiencing shooting pains in his back and pins and needles in his feet, leading to concerns he may have injured his spine. Meanwhile, 66-year-old Anthony, who has recently been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and prostate cancer, has taken a tumble down a flight of stairs at home. He's very frail and a scan reveals he has broken some ribs, puncturing a lung

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E
programme.desc: Former boxer Paul, 22, has been stabbed in the face and arm with a broken bottle outside a nightclub in Kingston. As the team works to stop the bleeding and treat the patient's wounds, his girlfriend Naveena reflects on his sensitive side. programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Comedian Chris Ramsey researches his family tree, starting by investigating his great grandfather who fought in the First World War. A trip to the military base in Dorset where he trained, reveals he fought at Gallipoli, one of the deadliest campaigns of the conflict. Tracing back to the late 18th century, Chris revisits the era when his five-times great grandmother was pregnant. These deadly new machines were created to hunt them down, but are now growing independent and intend to make use of technology from the Transformers' home planet in a plot that could threaten all life on Earth. Sci-fi adventure sequel, starring Mark Wahlberg, Anthony Hopkins, Gemma Chan, Stanley Tucci and John Turturro
